#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name="Scrape"
#SBATCH --mail-user=joel.niklaus@inf.unibe.ch
#SBATCH --mail-type=end,fail
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --time=15-00:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=256GB
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --qos=job_epyc2_long
#SBATCH --partition=epyc2

# Put your code below this line

python ejustice.py

# IMPORTANT:
# Run with                  sbatch run_ubelix_job.sh
# check with                squeue --user=jn20t930 --jobs={job_id}
# monitor with              scontrol show --detail jobid {job_id}
# cancel with               scancel {job_id}
# monitor gpu usage with    ssh gnode14 and then nvidia-smi
# run interactive job with  srun --partition=gpu-invest --gres=gpu:rtx3090:1 --mem=64G --time=02:00:00 --pty /bin/bash

issues: A comment in the script refers to monitoring GPU usage (`nvidia-smi`), but the job does not request any GPU resources (e.g., --gres=gpu:1). This comment is misleading for a CPU-only job.

The script calls `python` directly. This relies on the default environment of the compute node, which may vary. It is best practice to activate a specific virtual environment (e.g., `source venv/bin/activate`) or load a specific module (`module load python/3.x`) to ensure reproducibility.

The requested wall time (15 days) and memory (256GB) are very large. While syntactically correct, ensure these values are not overestimated, as this can significantly increase queue wait times and may impact other users.
